newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said the rates began to stabilise today after last Friday's losses with surging domestic A shares encouraging securities houses and brokerages to borrow on the market.

"Money supply on the market is still sufficient with state banks continuing to lend large amounts of money," said one trader. "But non-bank institutions have increased their borrowing significantly due to the active A share markets."

In addition, the Finance Ministry will issue 20 billion yuan worth of new treasury bonds next month and the institutions are borrowing money to prepare to bid for underwriting rights in a public tender late this month, traders said.
"Money demand on the market is expected to increase ahead of the issue of new seven-year bonds early next month," said a second trader. "This will prevent the rates from falling significantly."

The interbank rates have recently been on a slight downtrend because the People's Bank of China, the central bank, has promised to cut bank reserve ratios by a large margin this year, which will release large amounts of cash, traders said.
Beijing requires banks to save 13 percent of their deposits for the central bank and five to seven percent for themselves.
